finding: The L6 release attestation reader used ordinary json.loads for gate reports and trusted-producer configuration. Duplicate object keys could be silently overwritten, and non-finite JSON constants were accepted by the parser before later validation.
changes: Gate reports and trusted-producer configuration now use one strict JSON parser that rejects duplicate keys at every nesting level and rejects NaN/Infinity constants.
Gate report files must decode to a JSON object before they enter attestation validation; parse and shape failures fail closed as GateBlocked.

verification.pytest: tests/test_l6_attestation_json_integrity.py: 5 passed, including valid Q0-Q9 attestation round-trip
verification.ruff: passed for attestation.py and its regression selector

scope: Synthetic malformed report and configuration JSON only. No release gates were marked PASS and no external evidence, market, account, ledger, Validation, Test, or Holdout payload was read.
remaining: This closes the local ambiguous-JSON parsing gap for L6 attestation inputs. Hosted Linux/Windows CI and upstream authenticated evidence remain separate open gates.
